b06c728f385e31bb2480fc518074fb47e47d4290.summary: SecurityScorecard research page on the last version of REvil (Sodinokibi) ransomware. The text says the family has been active since 2019 with breaks due to law enforcement. It describes an RC4-encrypted configuration, killing a list of targeted processes, stopping some specified services, deleting Volume Shadow Copies, and targeting logical drives and network shares. Most of the page is site navigation. It names no actors, CVEs, sectors, countries or figures.

b0f478f447f65c4f77c981a3f5f3ce85274aa352.summary: Netresec blog post by Erik Hjelmvik (published 28 April 2025) on decoding njRAT remote access trojan traffic with the NetworkMiner tool, using a Triage sandbox run. It lists the artefacts NetworkMiner can extract from njRAT command-and-control traffic: victim screenshots, transferred files, C2 commands, bot replies, stolen credentials and keylog data. The text says njRAT has been in use since 2013 and that antivirus vendors call it Bladabindi. The post is a tutorial rather than a campaign report and names no threat actor.

dates.q: 2013, but despite being over 10 years old it still remains
dates.what: njRAT has been around since this year

tools.q: njRAT is a Remote Access Trojan (RAT) that can be used to remotely control a hacked computer.
Anti virus vendors usually refer to njRAT as Bladabindi.
NetworkMiner has a built-in parser for the njRAT Command-and-Control (C2) protocol.
I investigate network traffic from a Triage sandbox execution of njRAT in this video.
NetworkMiner in Linux (REMnux to be specific).
